# `css-modules/class-naming`

**CSS Module class names can be read as styles.name**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` (npm) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `style` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (renaming a class must update every file that reads it) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |

## What it checks

A class of a CSS Module is named so that JavaScript reads it as `styles.name`: camelCase by default. With `style = "kebab"` it is kebab-case instead, and `any` turns the check off.

**Why:** `.btn-primary` is `styles["btn-primary"]` and cannot be `styles.btn-primary`; a name that needs brackets is easy to mistype and is not found by a search for `styles.btnPrimary`.

The bundler's `localsConvention` (`[css] modules_convention`) counts: under `camelCase` or `dashes` a kebab-case class is reached as `styles.btnPrimary`, so it passes. Classes inside `:global(…)` are not checked.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css-modules
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css-modules/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css-modules/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css-modules/class-naming" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | `string` | `"camelCase"` | `camelCase` (a name `styles.x` reaches without brackets), `kebab` (kebab-case) or `any` (no check) |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."css-modules/class-naming"]
severity = "error"

[rules."css-modules/class-naming".options]
style = "camelCase"
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"css-modules/class-naming" = { severity = "error", options = { style = "styles.x" } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `style`

*string* · default `"camelCase"`

`camelCase` (a name `styles.x` reaches without brackets), `kebab` (kebab-case) or `any` (no check)

```toml
[rules."css-modules/class-naming".options]
style = "styles.x"
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css-modules/class-naming" = { options = { style = "styles.x" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css-modules/class-naming" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css-modules/class-naming" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css-modules/class-naming" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css-modules/class-naming" = { severity = "warn", options = { style = "styles.x" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css-modules/class-naming": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"style": "styles.x"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Also configured by `[css]`

CSS Modules: which stylesheets are modules, and how the bundler turns a class name into `styles.x`. Read by the `css-modules/*` rules and the project graph. Root config only.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `modules` | `array` | `[]` | Globs of CSS Module stylesheets besides `*.module.css` and `*.module.scss`, from the project root. |
| `modules_convention` | `asIs` · `camelCase` · `camelCaseOnly` · `dashes` · `dashesOnly` | `"asIs"` | css-loader's `localsConvention`: how a class such as `.btn-primary` is reached from JavaScript. `asIs`: `styles["btn-primary"]`; `camelCase`: that and `styles.btnPrimary`; `camelCaseOnly`: only `styles.btnPrimary`; `dashes` and `dashesOnly`: dashes become camel case, other characters stay. |

```toml
[css]
modules = ["src/**/*.styles.css"]
modules_convention = "camelCase"
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css-modules/class-naming: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css-modules/class-naming: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css-modules/class-naming expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css-modules/class-naming --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css-modules/class-naming       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css-modules/class-naming  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>            # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Rename the class (and every `styles.…` that reads it) to camelCase.
2. Or set `[css] modules_convention = "camelCase"` if the bundler already maps the names.

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.btn-primary { color: red; }
```

#### Do

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.btnPrimary { color: red; }
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.btn-primary { color: red; }
```

#### Do

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.btnPrimary { color: red; }
```
